subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What minimal core capability/grant model should OpenClaw standardize for skills and plugin-owned tools before contributors implement enforcement?
rationale: The source, related issues, and history show adjacent name-based policy and per-call approval mechanisms but no canonical capability taxonomy, grant store, enforcement boundary, or audit owner; choosing those shapes defines a public security boundary and plugin API contract.

options.title: Approve staged core capability layer
options.body: Define a small sensitive-capability taxonomy first, then add grant storage, filtering, execution checks, and audit records in separate PRs.

options.title: Limit to manifest visibility for now
options.body: Keep enforcement out of scope and use the narrower open RFC for declarative capability metadata only.

options.title: Keep governance plugin-only
options.body: Treat this as external runtime policy and close the core item once maintainers decide no new OpenClaw grant API is wanted.

recommendation.title: Approve staged core capability layer
recommendation.body: Define a small sensitive-capability taxonomy first, then add grant storage, filtering, execution checks, and audit records in separate PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security-boundary and gateway enforcement decision, and Peter has both adjacent gateway/security history and a prior issue comment keeping this broader item open.
